decisionMemo.businessProblem: A $1.8B not-for-profit, 5-hospital, 50-clinic health system has seen EBITDA margin collapse from 12.0% (FY2024) to 7.5% (FY2025), a 450 basis point compression, while net patient revenue stayed essentially flat ($1,790M → $1,800M, +0.6%). Total operating expense rose $90M (+5.7%) against only $10M of revenue growth. The cost growth is concentrated in labor — total labor up $90M (+11.1%) driven heavily by contract/agency nursing doubling from $70M to $140M — and in medical supplies & pharmacy, up $36M (+10%). At the same time, inpatient admissions fell 3% YoY (the higher-revenue, higher-fixed-cost setting) while outpatient volume grew only 2%. Reimbursement rates are externally set by Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial contracts, so the flat revenue reflects static rates and payer mix, not a pricing decision the system controls. The board faces a covenant/rating threshold near 8% EBITDA margin and must decide within ~90 days whether to cut agency staffing, restructure, or accept a downgrade. The core diagnostic question: is this margin erosion a cost-structure and labor-throughput problem (controllable operationally), a pricing/strategy problem, or a demand/forecasting problem — and what first action restores margin without breaching safe nurse-staffing ratios or harming quality?

Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)

Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
